title: Inserting Records
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of inserting records in a Classic ASP application.
Identify and describe at least two syllabus subtopics: Designing an INSERT operation and Reading validated form data.
Inspect a minimal example and define a reproducible normal-case and failure-case test.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study inserting records as part of Classic ASP development and legacy maintenance. The lesson follows the attached ASP curriculum topic 71 and uses the syllabus subtopics as the coverage checklist.
content.why_it_matters: Inserting Records matters because Classic ASP behavior crosses a server-side scripting engine, IIS configuration, request/response boundaries, and often COM or ADO dependencies. A small, explicit test helps distinguish intended behavior from runtime-specific behavior.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Classic ASP applications commonly use ADO to access relational databases through a provider. For 'Inserting Records', validate inputs, prefer `ADODB.Command` parameters for values, close Recordsets and Connections, and handle failures without exposing the query, connection string, or database details. Parameter syntax, supported types, cursor behavior, and connection string details can vary by provider; verify them against the installed driver and database.

content_blocks.title: Syllabus coverage
content_blocks.text: The lesson explicitly covers: Designing an INSERT operation; Reading validated form data; Inserting records through ADO; Using parameterized INSERT commands; Retrieving generated identifiers; Handling database constraints; Reporting failed submissions. Treat these subtopics as connected requirements. For each one, be able to define the concept, identify where it appears in a Classic ASP application, and name one test or diagnostic that would verify it.

content_blocks.title: Inspectable example: Inserting Records
content_blocks.code:
<%
Const adCmdText = 1
Const adParamInput = 1
Const adVarChar = 200
Dim cmd, displayName
displayName = Trim(Request.Form("displayName"))
If Len(displayName) < 1 Or Len(displayName) > 80 Then Response.End
Set cmd = Server.CreateObject("ADODB.Command")
Set cmd.ActiveConnection = conn
cmd.CommandType = adCmdText
cmd.CommandText = "INSERT INTO Student (DisplayName) VALUES (?)"
cmd.Parameters.Append cmd.CreateParameter("name", adVarChar, adParamInput, 80, displayName)
cmd.Execute
%>

content_blocks.title: Runtime and safety checkpoint
content_blocks.text: Use synthetic records in a local test database and a least-privilege database account. Record the database/provider version and verify both success and failure cases. The source syllabus treats Classic ASP as a legacy maintenance technology, not as ASP.NET or a default choice for new web projects.

content_blocks.title: Guided workflow
content_blocks.text: 1. Start with a minimal local example of inserting records. 2. Trace its inputs, state changes, dependencies, and output. 3. Test a normal case, a missing/malformed case, and one permission/provider/runtime failure. 4. Write down the exact expected and observed result before changing another variable.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating legacy runtime behavior as universal.
common_mistakes.why: IIS versions, Windows lifecycle, COM registration/bitness, and ADO providers can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Write down the actual server/provider versions and validate on a disposable test site.

common_mistakes.why: Empty input, missing records, expired sessions, permissions, timeouts, and malformed data reveal different failure modes.
common_mistakes.fix: Add normal, negative, and boundary cases with expected outcomes.

common_mistakes.why: Detailed errors can reveal paths, SQL text, configuration, and component information.
common_mistakes.fix: Keep diagnostics in restricted server-side logs and return a generic message with a reference ID.
